### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**52** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 55 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c6987cb674a9a6eddf4470ba96496e0a9af3a39f` — the merge of head `bec3326d5fec0554c455badbaabe535c27bc8e61` into base `36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c6987cb674a9a6eddf4470ba96496e0a9af3a39f && git checkout c6987cb674a9a6eddf4470ba96496e0a9af3a39f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802 bec3326d5fec0554c455badbaabe535c27bc8e61 && git checkout -B drift-repro 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802 && git merge --no-ff bec3326d5fec0554c455badbaabe535c27bc8e61

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 36c0e96aa0ad1195293a5997e96fb88341815802` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `bec3326d5fec0554c455badbaabe535c27bc8e61`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-11-16T05:10Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6907815215; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in a project thread for domain:server#5 (zhuangjianguo); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Face: the committed changesets carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, so this record is rendered on the declaration face. M1 below says that line is not true of this head; a head that re-declares the narrowing owes its review on the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and this record does not stand in for it. Read: all nine paths of the diff, plus, read and not reviewed, `scim-sso-adoption.ts`, `scim-identity-source.ts`, `scim-connection-service.ts`, `auth-manager.ts` (`reconcileScimUserLifecycle`) and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` at this head. The vendor package is not installed in the review container, so its behaviour is taken from the host's own notes and the dev's end-to-end suite.

### ① Derived judgments

Against the card's four terms:

- Term 1 (create, replace and patch set `manager_id` under the admin endpoint's four refusals, as SCIM errors): holds. `screenUserManagerLink` is extracted and imported, not copied; `applyUserManagerLink` calls the same function, and its moved body is unchanged. Each refusal is answered 400 `invalidValue` in RFC 7644 shape with the admin code, inside the SCIM transaction. The manager is looked up only among the Users the same connection provisioned, and an id of another connection gets the same answer as an unknown one. Self-reference is judged on the platform user, not on the SCIM id. Pinned end to end for self, cycle, depth, cross-organization, unknown, another connection, and "nothing written".
- Term 2 (unknown manager refused loudly): holds for the profile-source connection on an active user. It does not hold on two paths that answer 2xx and write nothing (S3).
- Term 3 (clearing the attribute clears `manager_id`): holds, and the head does more than the term says (M2).
- Term 4 (lint note and rule explanation): holds; the two rewritten pins assert the new sentence. One overstatement (N2).

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix) — the `Clause-②` line is false for this head. Both changesets and the PR body say `yes (widening)`; the PR's own re-measure lists eight requests served today and refused now, and the plugin-auth changeset body has a paragraph headed "Requests accepted before and refused now". AGENTS.md makes `(narrowing)` BREAKING, with its banner and exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker in the changeset; neither is present. This is the dev's `open_questions` entry, answered here: option A. Option B ships an undeclared narrowing. Option C contradicts card term 2 and, as the dev notes, still narrows. Under A the dogfood battery is owed on the final head.
- M2 (must-fix) — the projection writes more than the card and the changeset declare, and nothing pins it. (a) The column is cleared on any active SCIM write whose stored attributes carry no manager, including a write that never named the attribute, so a value another route put there is removed with a 2xx. The changeset declares a clear only for "a PATCH remove, or a replace without it", and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` at this head still says of a directory-held user that "a value the column already holds stays as it is". (b) The set of identities the projection writes is wider than the set the admin endpoint refuses (the two are decided by different predicates; the detail is in the seat's private notes). On the overlap both doors accept a write and each replaces the other's without a refusal. That is the last-writer-wins outcome `admin-set-user-manager.ts` refusal 5 names as the one the ruling rejected. Needed: one ownership rule that both doors read, the absent-attribute behaviour stated in the changeset, and a pin for each. Which door owns the overlap is a maintainer call (③).
- S1 (should-fix) — `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:101-107` and `content/docs/capabilities/approvals.mdx:19-21` are made false by this diff and are not in it. The dev reports a ready patch; it should land with the behaviour or have a named carrier before merge.
- S2 (should-fix) — the plugin-auth changeset says "an unrelated update is never refused over the org chart". The dev's own loose end 3 says otherwise: once a stored manager reference stops resolving, every active write on the report is refused until the directory resends or removes it. Either the unchanged short-circuit covers that case or the changeset says what happens.
- S3 (should-fix) — three declared "not projected" branches have no pin: outside a SCIM request, a profile source of another connection, and an inactive user projected on re-activation. The second and third also accept a request carrying `manager` and write nothing, which is the silent drop term 2 rules out; each needs a stated reason in the changeset or a refusal.
- N1 (nit) — a `$ref` whose last segment is not decodable is answered as a server error, not as `invalidValue`, unless the vendor rejects it first.
- N2 (nit) — the rule explanation and the lint note say "on every SCIM create, replace and patch"; the projection runs only for an active user from its profile-source connection. The `screenUserManagerLink` jsdoc says "Refusals 1 to 4" and lists five.

No prior ids: this is the first review of the PR.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/lint`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct for a non-protocol change, and it stays `patch` once the narrowing is declared. What is missing is the declaration itself (M1): the `(narrowing)` arm, the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition marker.

CI on this head: 66 check-runs, 53 success, 11 skipped, 2 failure (`Test UI` and its shard `Test UI (5/16)`). Nothing is still running. The diff touches no `ui/` path and the dev reports the failing case as an app-shell deep-link timeout, but the head is red as read; a later PASS needs that check green or re-run, not waved.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` Clause-② arm: answered, option A (M1). No maintainer ruling is needed for the arm itself; the card's term 2 already rules the strict refusal.
- Escalated to the maintainer: who owns `manager_id` for a SCIM-provisioned identity the admin endpoint does not refuse (M2b), and whether a SCIM write that never names `manager` may clear a value another route wrote (M2a). The ruling of record 6895645364 says the directory wins where a directory holds the identity; it does not say the directory also writes where it does not.
- Deviation, `validate-approval-approvers.test.ts` outside the claim surface: accepted. The two pins asserted the sentence term 4 makes false.
- Deviation, second shared export `writeUserManagerLink`: accepted. One write site, package-internal, and the tenant-audit census stays at one.
- Deviation, dependents' suites not run and the full plugin-auth suite not measured locally at this head: accepted on `Test Core` success for this head; the package's public exports are unchanged.
- Loose ends 1 and 2 (docs): S1. Loose end 3: S2. Loose end 4: S3. Loose end 5: M1.
- File surface: within the claim, apart from the accepted test file. ADR-0135 D4 stamping is untouched and runs first.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The projection adds keyed single-row reads; the chain walk is the existing helper, moved and not changed.
- Security discipline: mechanisms are kept out of this record.

### ④ Design judgment

The seam is right: one screen, one write, inside the vendor's transaction, with the manager resolved inside the acting connection only. The design gap is ownership. The card closes "no path changes it" for identities the admin endpoint refuses, and the head projects onto a wider set and treats "the directory says nothing" as "the directory says none". Both follow from projecting the stored state without asking who owns the column, and both are settled by the one rule M2 asks for.
